title: Generating pointing-trial rows
description: You can follow distance-width combinations into a four-column dataset.

steps.description: You define model coefficients, four distances and three widths. TRIALS requests 15 observations for each distance-width pair.
The nested loops compute ID as log2(D / W + 1). You generate a noisy modeled sample for the current pair.

steps.question: How many rows will all distance-width pairs contribute?
steps.answer: They contribute 180 rows: four distances times three widths times 15 trials.

steps.description: Each tuple stores D, W, ID and the bounded sample value. You see 180 pointing trials and an ID range of 1.00 to 6.02 bits.
